vision_features.image_context: A human hand (palm up) holding approximately 16 small round seeds, approximately 5–8 mm in diameter each. The seeds appear to be soybean seeds. They are arranged in two loose clusters in the palm. The background shows dry, brownish soil or plant debris.
vision_features.abnormalities:
1. Purple-to-dark-violet discoloration on seed surfaces: Approximately 8–10 of the 16 seeds show irregular, blotchy areas of deep purple to dark violet coloration. These marks vary from small patches (roughly 1–2 mm) to covering nearly the entire surface of some seeds (up to 5–6 mm across). The discolored areas are irregular and diffuse in shape, not sharply defined. The base color of the affected seeds remains pale yellow to cream, with the purple patches overlaid on this background. No distinct border or halo separates the purple area from the yellow base color — the transition is gradual. The texture of affected areas appears smooth and dry, consistent with the rest of the seed surface. No raised structures, powdery coating, or exudate is visible on the purple areas.
2. Dark elongated mark at the hilum: On at least 2–3 seeds, the hilum (the seed scar/attachment point) appears dark gray to black and slightly elongated, approximately 1–2 mm long. This is a linear, narrow mark centered on the hilum area.
3. Fully unaffected seeds: Approximately 4–5 seeds appear uniformly pale yellow-cream with no visible discoloration, appearing smooth and normal in color.
4. One seed shows a white, slightly opaque patch on its surface (upper cluster, center-right), roughly 2–3 mm, irregular in shape, with a slightly dull or chalky texture compared to the surrounding seed coat.
vision_features.absences:
1. No powdery or dusty coating is visible on any of the seed surfaces.
2. No shriveling, wrinkling, or collapsed seed coats are observed — all seeds appear fully rounded and plump.
3. No visible mold threads, fuzzy growth, or filamentous structures on any seed surface.
4. No cracking or splitting of the seed coat is visible on any of the seeds.
vision_features.summary: Approximately 16 small, round, pale yellow seeds are held in a human palm, with roughly half showing irregular blotchy patches of deep purple-to-violet discoloration covering portions of the seed surface. The discoloration varies from small spots to nearly full coverage of individual seeds, overlaid on a uniform pale yellow-cream base coat. A few seeds show a dark mark at the hilum area. The most striking feature is the vivid, irregular deep-purple blotching on the otherwise uniformly yellow seed coats. Seeds retain their plump, rounded shape with smooth, dry surfaces throughout.

Knowledge-base entry for 'Purple_Seed_Stain':
────────────────────────────────────────
Seeds may be symptomless or have pink to purple spots extending from the hilum. Crop value may be lowered by dockage or seed certification denial, but yield is not reduced.. Pink to purple spots extending from the hilum on the seed coat; seeds may also be completely symptomless.
────────────────────────────────────────

Knowledge-base entry for 'Bean_Pod_Mottle_virus':
────────────────────────────────────────
Virus infection causes diffusion of pigments from the seed hilum, resulting in mottling of the seed coat. Hilum color determines the color and intensity of seed coat discoloration.. Mottling of the seed coat due to pigment diffusion from the hilum; color and intensity of discoloration is determined by hilum color. Mottling is associated with poor germination.
────────────────────────────────────────

Knowledge-base entry for 'Phytophthora':
────────────────────────────────────────
Early symptoms include seed rot and damping off; the most characteristic symptom is a dark brown lesion on the lower stem extending up from the taproot, which can girdle the stem causing stunting or death.. A dark brown lesion on the lower stem extending up from the taproot, reaching as high as several nodes, girdling the stem; as disease progresses, damping off, stunting, yellowing, and brown lesions on lower stem can occur.. Diaporthe complex (stem canker), Fusarium root rot and wilt, Pythium seedling blight and root rot, Rhizoctonia seedling blight and root rot, Sudden death syndrome, White mold, Anthracnose stem blight, Brown stem rot, Charcoal rot, Herbicide injury, Early season frost damage, Insect and mite injury
────────────────────────────────────────

DISCRIMINATING: 'Purple_Seed_Stain' vs 'Bean_Pod_Mottle_virus'
Ruling feature : Pattern of discoloration: discrete pink-to-purple spots extending from the hilum (A) vs. diffuse mottling/bleed of pigment across the seed coat (B)
Purple_Seed_Stain: Seeds show distinct pink to purple spots that extend outward from the hilum, or may appear completely symptomless with no discoloration at all.
Bean_Pod_Mottle_virus: Seeds show a diffuse mottling of the seed coat caused by pigment bleeding/diffusion from the hilum, with color and intensity varying according to hilum color.
Decision rule  : IF the discoloration is a defined, localized pink-to-purple spot(s) radiating from the hilum (or the seed is symptomless), THEN suspect Purple Seed Stain (A); IF the discoloration is a diffuse, bleed-out mottling spread across the seed coat, THEN suspect Bean Pod Mottle Virus (B).
